# {.sidebar width="380px"}

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Everything the page needs is behind one module, because Observable cells
// can only load plain JavaScript through dynamic import(). Resolving the
// specifier against document.baseURI keeps it working under any deployment
// path, including a GitHub Pages project subfolder.
app = import(new URL("assets/js/app.js", document.baseURI).href)

catalog = app.loadCatalog()
variables = catalog.variables
statuses = catalog.statuses

// The selected profile row names its dataset; the plots need the catalog
// entry to know which observations file to register.
datasets_by_id = new Map(
  catalog.regions.flatMap((region) =>
    region.products.flatMap((product) =>
      product.datasets.map((entry) => [entry.id, entry])
    )
  )
)

// One row per published profile of the selected product, worst disagreement
// first. Both pages read this, so it is fetched once here rather than by
// whichever page happens to be open.
profile_rows = app.profileSummary(selection.datasets, row_limit)
```

```{ojs}
//| title: Regions and products
viewof selection = app.treeView(catalog)
```

```{ojs}
//| title: Rows
viewof row_limit = Inputs.select([100, 500, 2000], {
  label: "Profiles shown",
  value: 500
})
```

```{ojs}
//| title: Profiles

// The whole drill-down lives in this sidebar: region, then product, then
// profile. Both pages show what is selected here, so a reader can switch
// between the plots and the tables without losing their place, and can pick
// a different profile from either one.
//
// Three columns, because the sidebar is narrow. The full breakdown, every
// category for every variable, is the first table on the Tables page.
viewof profile_row = app.tableView(profile_rows, {
  columns: [
    { key: "profile_id", label: "Profile", align: "left", format: (value) => value },
    { key: "n_obs", label: "Obs", title: "Observations in the profile" },
    {
      key: "n_disagree",
      label: "Disagree",
      title: "Observations the two sources disagree on"
    }
  ],
  rowKey: "profile_id",
  sortKey: "n_disagree",
  autoSelect: true,
  empty: "No profiles were published for this product."
})
```

# Plots {orientation="rows"}

## Row

```{ojs}
//| title: Profile

// Measurement on the x axis, pressure down the y axis, one marker per
// observation coloured by which source flagged it. Scroll or drag to zoom;
// double click to reset. Zooming and panning stop at the edge of the data.
{
  if (!profile_row) {
    return htl.html`<p class="nq-empty">Select a profile in the sidebar.</p>`;
  }
  const entry = datasets_by_id.get(profile_row.dataset_id);
  const observations = await app.profileObservations(entry, profile_row.profile_id);

  const box = document.createElement("div");
  box.className = "nq-profile";
  box.appendChild(
    htl.html`<p class="nq-meta"><strong>${profile_row.profile_id}</strong>
      ${entry.label} &middot; ${profile_row.n_obs} observations</p>`
  );
  // The colour key rides at the top of this panel, above the markers it
  // explains and inside the same card, so it is on screen whatever the plots
  // do below it. Five categories take one row on a wide window and two on a
  // narrow one.
  box.appendChild(
    htl.html`<div class="nq-plot-legend">${app.statusLegend(statuses)}</div>`
  );
  const plots = document.createElement("div");
  plots.className = "nq-plots";
  for (const variable of variables) {
    plots.appendChild(
      await app.profilePlot(observations, { variable, statuses })
    );
  }
  box.appendChild(plots);
  return box;
}
```

## Row {height="300px"}

```{ojs}
//| title: aiqclib QC checks that flagged

// Under the plots, because it answers the question they raise: when aiqclib
// marked something the input did not, which of its checks was it? "Fired" is
// what the code calls it; this is the same thing said plainly. The title
// names aiqclib because the page carries two sets of flags, and a panel of
// flag values headed "QC check" could be read as either of them.
{
  if (!profile_row) {
    return htl.html`<p class="nq-empty">Select a profile in the sidebar.</p>`;
  }
  const entry = datasets_by_id.get(profile_row.dataset_id);
  const rows = await app.profileItemBreakdown(entry, profile_row.profile_id);

  // One table per variable, in the catalog's order, which is the order the
  // plots above are drawn in. A single table mixed the two together and left
  // the reader matching `psal_` prefixes by eye against the plot they were
  // actually looking at.
  const blocks = variables.map((variable) => {
    // A check that judges the whole profile, its date or its pressure, feeds
    // both computed flags, so it belongs under both variables rather than in
    // a third table off to the side.
    const shaped = rows
      .filter((row) => app.checkAppliesTo(row.item, variable, variables))
      .map((row) => ({ ...row, check: app.qcCheck(row.item, variables).label }));

    const table = app.tableView(shaped, {
      columns: [
        {
          key: "check",
          label: "QC check",
          align: "left",
          title: "The aiqclib test that raised the flag, and the column it writes",
          // The name in words, with the column it writes under it: the same
          // pairing the contingency table heads its axes with. Under rather
          // than beside, because a column of its own pushed the counts off
          // the side of a table this narrow.
          //
          // Linked rather than described: eleven descriptions do not fit a
          // panel this short, and the About page already carries them. The
          // href is the rendered page, because Quarto rewrites `.qmd` links
          // in markdown and this node is built in the browser.
          render: (value, row) =>
            htl.html`<div><a href="about.html#the-checks-aiqclib-runs"
              title="${app.checkNote(row.item, variables)}">${value}</a>
              <span class="nq-colname">${row.item}</span></div>`
        },
        {
          key: "flag",
          label: "Flag",
          format: app.flagWithMeaning,
          title: "The flag the check raised, worst in the profile first"
        },
        { key: "n", label: "Obs", title: "Observations the check flagged" }
      ],
      rowKey: "item",
      sortKey: "n",
      selectable: false,
      empty: `No aiqclib check flagged ${variable.label.toLowerCase()} here.`
    });
    return htl.html`<section class="nq-qc-block">
      <p class="nq-meta">${variable.label}</p>
      ${table}</section>`;
  });

  // Three narrow columns across the full width of the page leave the counts a
  // long way from the name they belong to, so each table keeps its own width
  // and the two sit beside each other while the window has room for both.
  // The line above them says whose flags these are: the plots draw both
  // sources at once, and nothing else in the panel would say that this
  // breakdown belongs to only one of them.
  return htl.html`<div class="nq-qc-items">
    <p class="nq-note">A check that judges the whole profile is listed under
      both variables, because both computed flags take it in.</p>
    <div class="nq-qc-row">${blocks}</div></div>`;
}
```

# Tables {orientation="rows"}

## Row {height="250px"}

```{ojs}
//| title: Profile summary

// The selected profile alone, one row per variable and one column per
// agreement category. The sidebar is the profile list; repeating every
// profile of the product here spent the top of the page on rows the reader
// had not asked about, and pushed the numbers that do belong to their
// profile out to the far edge.
{
  if (!profile_row) {
    return htl.html`<p class="nq-empty">Select a profile in the sidebar.</p>`;
  }
  const entry = datasets_by_id.get(profile_row.dataset_id);
  const flagged = statuses.filter((status) => status.flagged);

  const rows = variables.map((variable, order) => {
    // The catalog's own order, which is also the order the plots are drawn
    // in, so the two pages read the variables the same way round.
    const row = { order, name: variable.name, label: variable.label };
    for (const status of statuses) {
      row[status.key] = Number(
        profile_row[`${variable.name}_n_${status.key}`] ?? 0
      );
    }
    row.n_flagged = flagged.reduce((sum, status) => sum + row[status.key], 0);
    return row;
  });

  const box = document.createElement("div");
  box.className = "nq-profile-summary";
  box.appendChild(
    htl.html`<p class="nq-meta"><strong>${profile_row.profile_id}</strong>
      ${entry.label} &middot; ${app.formatTime(profile_row.profile_timestamp)}
      &middot; ${app.formatCount(profile_row.n_obs)} observations,
      ${app.formatCount(profile_row.n_disagree)} of them disagreements</p>`
  );
  const row = document.createElement("div");
  row.className = "nq-summary-row";
  row.appendChild(
    app.tableView(rows, {
      columns: [
        {
          key: "label",
          label: "Variable",
          align: "left",
          format: (value) => value
        },
        {
          key: "n_flagged",
          label: "Flagged mix",
          align: "left",
          title: "How the flagged observations split between the cases",
          // Over the flagged categories alone: drawn over all five it would
          // be one block of "neither flagged" on every row.
          render: (value, row) =>
            app.compositionBar(
              flagged.map((status) => ({
                label: status.label,
                value: row[status.key],
                color: status.color
              })),
              { empty: "nothing flagged in this profile" }
            )
        },
        ...statuses.map((status) => ({
          key: status.key,
          label: status.label,
          title: `Observations of this profile: ${status.label.toLowerCase()}`
        }))
      ],
      rowKey: "name",
      sortKey: "order",
      descending: false,
      selectable: false,
      empty: "No variables are published for this product."
    })
  );
  // The bar is the only thing on this page that says anything in colour, so
  // its key belongs beside it rather than one tab away. A column rather than
  // a row: the space left over next to a table this narrow is tall, not wide.
  row.appendChild(
    htl.html`<aside class="nq-summary-key">${app.statusLegend(statuses)}</aside>`
  );
  box.appendChild(row);
  return box;
}
```

## Row

```{ojs}
//| title: Contingency

// The cross-tabulation the whole project is about: how the input's flag value
// and the value aiqclib computed line up, for this profile alone.
{
  const box = document.createElement("div");
  if (!profile_row) {
    box.className = "nq-empty";
    box.textContent = "Select a profile in the sidebar.";
    return box;
  }
  const entry = datasets_by_id.get(profile_row.dataset_id);
  box.appendChild(
    htl.html`<p class="nq-meta"><strong>${profile_row.profile_id}</strong>
      ${entry.label} &middot; ${profile_row.n_obs} observations</p>`
  );
  // The tables name both flag columns in words and gloss the values the
  // scheme fixes, which leaves one thing on the page unexplained: the red.
  // That is a setting of the build rather than anything the scheme says, so
  // it is written out here instead of left to a tooltip nobody hovers. Above
  // the tables, because a key read after the table it explains is a key read
  // twice, and because this is the shortest thing in the panel.
  box.appendChild(
    htl.html`<p class="nq-note">Under each flag value is what the IOC/Argo
      scheme calls it. Red marks the input values this product counts as an
      anomaly, which is a setting of the build, not of the scheme;
      <a href="about.html">About</a> explains both.</p>`
  );
  // Side by side while the window is wide enough for both, because a
  // cross-tabulation of a handful of values is a short, narrow thing and
  // stacking them put the second one under the fold. They stack again when
  // the space for two is gone.
  const side = document.createElement("div");
  side.className = "nq-contingency-row";
  for (const variable of variables) {
    const rows = await app.profileContingency(entry, profile_row.profile_id, variable);
    const block = document.createElement("section");
    block.className = "nq-contingency-block";
    block.appendChild(htl.html`<p class="nq-meta">${variable.label}</p>`);
    block.appendChild(app.contingencyTable(rows, { variable }));
    side.appendChild(block);
  }
  box.appendChild(side);
  return box;
}
```
